featured.name: Sirius
featured.fact: The brightest star in the night sky. A white dwarf, Sirius B, circles it every 50 years.

featured.name: Betelgeuse
featured.fact: In 2019–20 it faded to about a third of its usual brightness, veiled mostly by dust from gas it threw off.

featured.name: Rigel
featured.fact: A blue supergiant. Though labelled beta, it is almost always brighter than Betelgeuse, Orion’s alpha.

featured.name: Aldebaran
featured.fact: Pioneer 10 is coasting its way, but Aldebaran recedes over four times faster, so the probe will never arrive.

source: Yale Bright Star Catalogue, 5th revised ed. (Hoffleit & Warren 1991), CDS catalogue V/50; facts: see docs/night-sky-facts.md
